past_medical_history: Cervical spondylosis with prior cervical discectomy (C5-C6, 3 years ago)

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait instability, 'brain fog,' and urinary incontinence for 11 months; concern about whether this is NPH or Alzheimer's given family history
patient.history_present_illness: A 66-year-old right-handed woman with hypothyroidism, hypertension, and a history of cervical discectomy at C5-C6 three years ago (with good postoperative recovery and only residual mild right arm paresthesias on gabapentin) was admitted for NPH evaluation. Over the past 11 months she has developed three progressive symptoms: (1) Gait instability — her husband describes a 'magnetic' gait with small shuffling steps that has progressively worsened; she has fallen twice. The gait change concerns her orthopedic surgeon because it is different from the gait abnormality she had from her cervical disease preoperatively, which was more spastic. (2) Cognitive decline — she describes 'brain fog,' difficulty multitasking, and forgetting where she put objects. She scored 22/30 on MoCA at outpatient clinic. Her family history of Alzheimer's (mother) makes her very anxious about this symptom. (3) Urinary urgency with occasional incontinence — she describes the need to rush to the bathroom and has had several near-miss accidents. Her thyroid was checked 3 months ago: TSH 1.8 (euthyroid on current dose). Brain MRI outpatient showed ventriculomegaly with Evans index 0.32 and borderline callosal angle of 88 degrees. The referring neurologist is concerned this could be NPH but notes the prior cervical spine surgery as a potential alternative explanation for gait changes.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x4. MoCA 22/30 — loses on memory (3/5 delayed recall), trail-making B, and clock drawing. Mild word-finding hesitancy. No aphasia.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild right arm weakness 4+/5 (attributed to residual C5-C6 radiculopathy). Lower extremity strength 5/5 bilaterally. Mild bilateral lower extremity tone increase.
neurological_exam.sensory: Right C6 dermatomal sensory reduction (residual radiculopathy). Vibration mildly reduced at ankles bilaterally. No Lhermitte sign.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally. Right brachioradialis diminished (chronic radiculopathy). Patellar 2+ bilaterally. Achilles 1+ bilaterally. No hyperreflexia in lower extremities. Plantar flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose intact. Heel-shin mildly awkward bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, shuffling gait. Reduced foot clearance. Short step length. Not spastic (distinct from prior cervical myelopathy gait). TUG 24 seconds. 10-meter walk 19 seconds.
neurological_exam.additional: No clonus. No Babinski. Neck range of motion mildly limited but no myelopathy signs. Lhermitte sign absent.

signal_characteristics.description: Moderate tight sulci at high convexity with sylvian fissure widening
Post-surgical changes at C5-C6 with no cord compression

mri.impression: 1. Brain MRI: Moderate ventriculomegaly; Evans index 0.32. Callosal angle 88 degrees on coronal T1. Moderate tight high-convexity sulci with Sylvian fissure widening. Mild periventricular FLAIR changes. 2. Cervical spine MRI: Post-surgical changes at C5-C6; no cord compression or signal change identified at this level. Clinical correlation recommended.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 16 cmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 42 mg/dL. Glucose: 62 mg/dL (ratio 0.67). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 668 pg/mL (borderline low-normal). total_tau: 242 pg/mL (borderline elevated). phospho_tau: 52 pg/mL (borderline; reference <61).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with gait analysis

findings.gait_description: Post-tap: improved initiation, slightly better step height, less wide-based; gait not spastic (confirms NPH gait, not cervical myelopathy pattern)

specialized_test.impression: High-volume tap trial (40 mL): TUG improved from 24 seconds pre-tap to 19 seconds at 24 hours (21% improvement). 10-meter walk improved from 19 to 15.5 seconds at 24 hours (18% improvement). MoCA improved 1 point at 24 hours. Post-tap gait: improved initiation, slightly improved step height, less wide-based. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: Borderline positive amyloid PET — CL score 28 (above threshold of 24.4)

output.impression: Positive — moderate-to-frequent amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 28 (above the amyloid positivity threshold of 24.4 CL). Clinical correlation recommended.

Phase-contrast MRI (aqueductal CSF flow): peak velocity 20 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); net stroke volume 58 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Hyperdynamic aqueductal CSF pulsatility identified. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: Moderately impaired — encoding and retrieval deficits

quantitative_data.pattern: Mixed NPH (frontal-subcortical) and possible early AD (memory > executive function impairment)

output.impression: Neuropsychological evaluation demonstrates mildly-to-moderately impaired executive function, moderately impaired episodic memory (encoding and retrieval deficits), mild word-finding difficulty, and moderately impaired processing speed. Profile shows mixed frontal-subcortical and amnestic features. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity at 140 mL fill

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity identified: involuntary detrusor contractions at 140 mL fill. Maximum cystometric capacity 260 mL. No urodynamic evidence of outlet obstruction. Clinical correlation recommended.

Extended lumbar drainage (72 hours): progressive gait improvement — TUG from 24 seconds baseline to 17.8 seconds at day 3 (26% improvement). MoCA improved 2 points at day 3. Clinical correlation recommended.

interactions: Gabapentin: continue perioperatively to prevent acute withdrawal (seizure risk) and rebound pain
warnings: Do not abruptly stop gabapentin — taper if discontinuation desired post-shunt

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. Small sharp spikes of sleep, a benign normal variant.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

differential.key_features: Family history, memory impairment, borderline amyloid PET — but classic NPH triad, positive tap trial, and DESH pattern support NPH as primary diagnosis; NPH-AD copathology likely
Prior C5-C6 discectomy — but cervical MRI shows no cord compression, gait post-tap is magnetic not spastic, no hyperreflexia or Babinski
Known hypothyroidism — but TSH 1.8, euthyroid on current levothyroxine dose

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Evans 0.32, callosal angle 88, DESH; cervical cord normal

optimal_actions.action: High-volume tap trial with gait analysis
Amyloid PET given family history and borderline CSF biomarkers
Extended lumbar drainage for equivocal tap
VP shunt with counseling regarding amyloid copathology

critical_actions: Confirm euthyroid status — hypothyroid cognitive impairment must be excluded
Cervical spine MRI to exclude recurrent myelopathy — no cord compression found
Amyloid PET is important given family history and borderline CSF biomarkers
NPH tap trial and extended drainage confirm treatable NPH component
Counsel patient that borderline positive amyloid PET suggests some Alzheimer's copathology may limit cognitive benefit of shunting
contraindicated_actions: Attributing gait disorder to recurrent cervical myelopathy without imaging
Withholding tap trial due to prior cervical surgery
Attributing cognitive decline to hypothyroidism when thyroid function is confirmed normal
key_reasoning_points: The moderate difficulty is the competing diagnoses: prior cervical myelopathy (recurrence excluded by MRI), hypothyroidism (excluded by normal TSH), family history of AD (borderline amyloid PET suggests early copathology)
Cervical spine MRI is important in patients with prior cervical surgery presenting with new gait symptoms
Gait quality post-tap (magnetic, not spastic) helps distinguish NPH gait from cervical myelopathy gait
Borderline amyloid PET and borderline CSF biomarkers in patient with family history of AD represent the moderate-difficulty element requiring careful communication with patient about prognosis

red_herrings.data_point: History of cervical discectomy C5-C6 with residual arm paresthesias
red_herrings.intended_effect: New gait deterioration attributed to recurrent cervical myelopathy
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Cervical MRI shows no recurrent cord compression; gait pattern is magnetic (NPH) not spastic (myelopathy)

red_herrings.intended_effect: Cognitive decline attributed to undertreated hypothyroidism
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: TSH 1.8 confirms euthyroid state on current levothyroxine — hypothyroid cognitive impairment excluded

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Moderate NPH with prior cervical surgery (myelopathy red herring), known hypothyroidism (cognitive red herring), family history of AD, and borderline amyloid PET suggesting NPH-AD copathology.
